purpose: Connect the existing GPU facial-scale signal to the Blender 085 virtual camera through a local atomic JSON state using a virtual P0 baseline without claiming absolute physical depth.

activities.label: reuse the VIZZ 084 two-ruler scale estimator and stream calibrated distance state
poll local state and update the Blender 085 controller without rendering or executing payloads

queries.expression: does the webcam-derived relative ratio control observer_distance_m only after explicit P0
does an invalid face or contradictory facial rulers leave the Blender camera unchanged
does the bridge avoid network, input injection and raw-video persistence

assumptions: P0 is an explicit virtual baseline; the experiment uses relative scale and does not claim absolute physical distance.
The existing VIZZ 084 GPU tracker and local RetinaFace model are available.
A local file is sufficient for the first two-process bridge and has lower surface area than a socket.
The Blender 085 scene is open before the bridge is installed.
kill_tests: No P0 means the live runner does not start.
Missing face or contradictory rulers produce UNKNOWN.
UNKNOWN never updates the Blender controller.
Partial JSON writes are prevented by atomic replacement.
No raw video, network access, input injection or remote execution is allowed.
unknowns: Whether the live webcam signal is stable enough during unconstrained work.
Whether the user prefers camera movement, display scaling or both.
Whether interactive Cycles viewport rendering is fast enough on the configured device.
Whether the single P0 meter reading remains sufficient for multiple monitors or head poses.
